newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Friday in moderate trade on interbank and interbank interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slighty lower but bond prices were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.58/1.53 percent compared with Thursday's yield of 1.73/1.68 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.60/1.55 against 1.65/1.60 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$99.40/99.45 from Thursday's close of S$99.25/99.30, September 2001 at S$99.46/99.51 versus S$99.38/99.43 and June 2003 at S$99.15/99.20 against S$99.04/99.09.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 2-7/8 2-3/4 percent from 2-3/4 2-5/8 percent.
